summary: Phase 149O.20J.8 -- Class-B writesecurity/chown ACL-Right Reclassification Repair Independent Verification: independently verified 149O.20J.7's repair of the remaining known-safe-vocabulary gap in B-149O.20J.4-1 without trusting J.7's report, tests, vocabulary audit, writesecurity/chown reasoning, Fast Green attribution, or historical-test-pinning justification. Reconstructed the exact production diff: true immediate parent of repair commit 26545b90 is 71613327 (git rev-parse 26545b90^); git diff 71613327 26545b90 -- src/ touches exactly hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py; an AST function-by-function diff (ast.dump per FunctionDef) confirms every function byte-identical except the two frozenset literals and comments; hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py and hatp_class_b_conformance.py byte-identical before/after. Re-derived HBDC's authority criterion directly from HBDC-REQ-016/017/020 and CBD-1/CBD-3 (docs/contracts/HATP_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md), independently of J.7's paraphrase. Independently re-typed the complete 21-member macOS ACL right inventory from man chmod's ACL MANIPULATION OPTIONS section (read fresh on this host) before comparing to production -- exactly equals production's combined _MACOS_ACL_KNOWN_RIGHTS; ground-truth-confirmed via real chmod +a + ls -le that the man page's hyphenated 'write-security' inheritance-example spelling does not match real canonical output (which always renders unhyphenated 'writesecurity', the token production's vocabulary actually matches). Independently adjudicated writesecurity as dangerous (man chmod: 'Write an object's security information (ownership, mode, ACL)' -- a holder can rewrite the object's own ACL to self-grant write/add_file/delete_child/etc. or flip mode bits directly, transitively write-equivalent under HBDC-REQ-016/020's own directory-entry-replacement logic) and chown as dangerous (man chmod: 'Change an object's ownership' -- new owner gets unconditional S_IWUSR mode-bit write authority with no ACL grant required at all; this single-user host's same-owner state does not substitute for that broader claim), from primary semantics independently, not from J.7's wording. Real fresh chmod +a fixtures (not copied from J.7; file and directory; mode bits set to deny owner-write so the ACL branch is genuinely exercised; PATH restricted to /usr/bin:/bin, independently confirmed necessary since this dev host's ordinary PATH makes _resolve_trusted_executable('ls') return None otherwise) confirm parser detection True in all four combinations. Exercised ancestor-chain composition (_ancestor_chain_safe) at a grandparent and a 3-levels-deep great-grandparent for both rights -- both reject with the correct offending ancestor named; the fully-safe control case used a real pre-existing root-owned file (/bin/ls, not a self-owned constructed fixture, which cannot demonstrate reaching the true boundary) -- reaches the filesystem root (ancestor_walk_reached_filesystem_root). Trusted-Git (_resolve_trusted_executable_with_effective_access) and Protected-Root (_check_ancestor_chain) composition both reject dangerous-ACL ancestors for both rights via the identical shared _ancestor_chain_safe primitive (confirmed via inspect.getsource); a real file-level write ACL directly on the candidate Git executable (J-3 core regression) also rejects. Independently audited all 11 remaining known-safe rights semantically (man-page definition, direct/transitive capability classification) BEFORE consulting the parser -- never used the parser as its own classification oracle; set-exhaustiveness confirmed equal to live _MACOS_ACL_KNOWN_SAFE_RIGHTS; each right's real grant confirmed parser-safe only as post-hoc confirmation. Fresh inheritance-modifier combination/masking check: add_file,file_inherit / writesecurity,directory_inherit / chown,limit_inherit / delete,only_inherit real grants all correctly detected dangerous=True (a dangerous sibling right in the same ACE is never masked by a co-occurring inherit modifier, since the parser checks membership across every comma-separated right in the entry); pure-modifier/pure-safe combinations correctly remain False. Independently confirmed execute/search and read/list contextual aliases (ground-truth chmod +a: execute on a directory renders as search; search on a file renders as execute) have no gap, since both spellings of each pair are already in the safe set. Unknown-right fail-closed regression (simulated via crafted ls-output stub, since real chmod rejects unknown tokens at the OS level): unknown alone/+safe/+dangerous/+inherit-modifier all correctly None, critically never masked-safe (False) when co-occurring with a dangerous right. Principal resolution (current user True; unrelated user daemon False; unresolvable user/group None; malformed shape None; an actual effective group True; unrelated group _postfix False) and allow/deny safety-direction (deny-only False; allow+deny same principal same dangerous right still True -- deny never suppresses a matching allow, conservative false-positive-unsafe only, never false-negative-safe; allow-other+deny-agent False) independently regressed fresh. Re-tested all established dangerous rights (directory: add_file, add_subdirectory, delete_child, delete, writesecurity, chown; file: write, append, writeextattr, writesecurity, chown) -- all detected True. Adjudicated J.7's J.6 historical-test-pin diff: git diff confirms exactly one test modified, now fetching the real historical blob via git show 4c4fd16d:... rather than asserting against the live module; independently confirmed 4c4fd16d is genuinely J.6's own commit and a strict ancestor of J.7's parent (git merge-base --is-ancestor); the pinned assertion is factually true against a freshly re-fetched copy of that historical blob; no other J.6 assertion was touched; all 67 J.6 tests pass against current production. Classification: legitimate historical snapshot pinning -- not evidence laundering, not mere benign supersession (git-verified byte-identical historical pin, stronger than a paraphrase). B-149O.20J.2-1 regression: writable grandparent behind a safe parent still rejects the full chain -- no early stop reappears. J-1: .pth tab-delimited import-line classification still correct (mirrors CPython's site.addpackage). J-2: os.getgroups() mocked empty -- _current_agent_identity() still independently includes the real os.getegid(). J-3 core: real file-level write ACL on the Git executable itself and a real ACL-only higher ancestor (three levels up) both reject through the complete-chain parser; historical scope preserved as previously narrowed, not restored to any earlier overbroad claim. Symlink/error/indeterminate regression: symlinked ancestor component rejects (ancestor_symlink diagnostic); malformed ACL line and ACL-tool nonzero-exit both None; indeterminate-ACL-tooling-only ancestor above a locally-mode-safe subject correctly None, never True (required tmp_path.resolve() to avoid this host's /tmp-to-/var symlink hop being correctly detected as an unrelated real symlink ancestor first -- a test-construction detail, not a production defect); the _stub_outside test-isolation helper itself independently verified to only affect paths outside its declared boundary. Fixed pre-J.7 baseline established via isolated git worktree add at 71613327 (J.7's true parent; not git stash, not the current failing-set used as its own oracle; PYTHONPATH pointed at the worktree's own src/ to avoid the editable-install path pointing back at the main repo). Broad Class-B/HBDC/J sweep on the baseline worktree: 11 failed / 725 passed / 5 skipped / 1 pre-existing collection error -- exactly matches J.7's own reported clean-baseline count, independently reproduced via a wholly different mechanism (isolated worktree, not git stash). Same sweep on current committed HEAD (including this phase's own new test file): one run gave the identical 11 failures (same exact node IDs), a second run gave 12 with one extra (test_real_host_invocation_does_not_mutate_repo_or_cwd_state), confirmed via isolated rerun to pass cleanly alone -- an order/parallelism-dependent flake under -n auto, not a dirty-tree artifact (repo was clean throughout) and not attributable to any committed change. Exact node-ID delta attributable to J.7 or J.8: zero. Fast Green (pytest -m fast_green -n auto, fido2 module ignored -- pre-existing/unrelated) on the baseline worktree: 72 failed / 6770 passed / 5 skipped / 1 pre-existing collection error, exact node IDs captured to a file. Current HEAD final captured run: 72 raw failed; exact-set comparison against the baseline shows precisely one node in, one node out, both inside tests/test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence, confirmed via isolated rerun of that entire test class to pass cleanly (7/7) -- an order/parallelism flake wholly unrelated to Class-B/ACL logic and to any file this phase or J.7 touched. HMIC frozen scope reconfirmed fresh (25 files, none of the three Class-B modules; 5 contract identity members) -- HMIC not modified by this phase. Read-only wall reconfirmed via AST scan of all three modules for mkdir/makedirs/chmod/chown/unlink/rmdir/rename/replace/symlink/link/write_text/write_bytes attribute access -- zero found in any module. Real-host result reconfirmed: verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() on this real, deliberately unprovisioned host is NON_COMPLIANT; git status --porcelain -- src/ identical (empty) immediately before and after the call.
